t: sumiie24 School-Management-System parent_Registration.php sql injection
d: A vulnerability has been found in sumiie24 School-Management-System up to d946d649c7c95e101fc5679ecd91999533bb10d7. The affected element is an unknown function of the file parent_Registration.php. Such manipulation of the argument student_reg leads to sql injection. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit has been disclosed to the public and may be used. This product implements a rolling release for ongoing delivery, which means version information for affected or updated releases is unavailable.

An uncontrolled recursion vulnerability exists in the LINE iOS app prior to version 26.19.0. The Flex Message processing component does not adequately validate the structure of externally supplied message content. As a result, an attacker who is able to send a crafted message to a victim could cause the application to crash when the message is received or displayed. A server-side mitigation has been deployed that also protects existing iOS clients that have not been updated to version 26.19.0.

t: sofastack sofa-bolt Hessian2 Deserialization HessianSerializer.java HessianSerializer.deserialize allocation of resources
d: A security flaw has been discovered in sofastack sofa-bolt up to 1.6.12. Affected by this issue is the function HessianSerializer.deserialize of the file src/main/java/com/alipay/remoting/serialization/HessianSerializer.java of the component Hessian2 Deserialization. Performing a manipulation results in allocation of resources. The attack can be initiated remotely. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

t: Org.keycloak:keycloak-services: org.keycloak:keycloak-server-spi-private: account resource sharing grants scopes outside the resource definition
d: A flaw was found in Keycloak. The Account API endpoint for sharing resources fails to verify whether owner-managed access is enabled and accepts permission scopes not assigned to the resource. An authenticated user can exploit this vulnerability to generate pre-granted permission tickets, causing Keycloak to bypass policy evaluation and issue access tokens with unauthorized scopes.

t: Org.keycloak:keycloak-services: uma issues fresh rpts for disabled resource-server clients
d: A flaw was found in Keycloak. When processing token requests using the User-Managed Access (UMA) grant, Keycloak fails to verify whether a target client or resource server is enabled before issuing an authorization token. An authenticated remote user can exploit this flaw to obtain valid Requesting Party Tokens (RPTs) for disabled clients, bypassing administrative access controls and permissions restrictions.

t: Org.keycloak.services.resources: client minimum acr (level of authentication) is not enforced when the login starts at the credential reset endpoint, allowing a
d: A flaw was found in Keycloak. When a client application enforces step-up authentication or multi-factor authentication (MFA) via a minimum authentication level, Keycloak fails to apply this requirement to login sessions initiated through the credential reset endpoint. An attacker who possesses a user's initial credentials (such as a password) can navigate from the reset interface back to the standard login form and authenticate without completing the required second factor. This flaw allows an attacker to obtain valid access tokens and gain unauthorized access to protected services without satisfying mandatory security controls.

t: Org.keycloak:keycloak-services: pre-revocation id tokens can mint fresh uma rpts after realm not-before
d: A flaw was found in Keycloak. When an administrator revokes tokens by setting a not-before revocation cutoff, Keycloak fails to enforce this boundary when processing User-Managed Access (UMA) grant requests using ID token claims. An authenticated remote user with an active session can submit a previously revoked ID token to receive a fresh Requesting Party Token (RPT). This flaw allows an attacker to bypass token revocation and retain unauthorized access to protected resources.

t: smartalock wireguard-lwip Session Index Allocator wireguard.c wireguard_generate_unique_index allocation of resources
d: A vulnerability was detected in smartalock wireguard-lwip up to cfba91666590e86bd67842c71cedf9a423be823a. This affects the function wireguard_generate_unique_index of the file src/wireguard.c of the component Session Index Allocator. The manipulation of the argument receiver_index results in allocation of resources. The attack is only possible with local access. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

The Canva Desktop App before 1.128.0 stores encrypted application state on disk. The encryption key is hardcoded as a plaintext string in the main.js file and is identical across all Canva installations on Windows and macOS.

t: BeamNG.drive before 0.40.6 LuaJIT FFI Sandbox Escape via JIT Bounds-Check Bypass
d: BeamNG.drive before 0.40.6 contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability because JIT-compiled LuaJIT traces omit FFI array bounds checks, letting untrusted Lua escape the sandbox. Attackers supplying a malicious mod can JIT-compile an FFI store loop, write out of range using a tostring() address leak, re-enable ffi.load, and run commands as the game user.

t: lwext4 through 1.0.0 Heap Buffer Overflow via ext4_fs_init_inode_bitmap
d: lwext4 through 1.0.0 contains a heap buffer overflow in ext4_fs_init_inode_bitmap() in src/ext4_fs.c because it does not validate s_inodes_per_group against the inode bitmap size. Attackers can supply a crafted ext4 image with an oversized s_inodes_per_group so memset writes past the heap buffer, corrupting memory and crashing the mounting application.

t: lwext4 through 1.0.0 Out-of-Bounds Write via ext4_fs_init_block_bitmap
d: lwext4 through 1.0.0 contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in ext4_fs_init_block_bitmap() that allows attackers to corrupt heap memory via crafted superblock geometry fields. Attackers can supply an ext4 image with oversized s_reserved_gdt_blocks and BLOCK_UNINIT groups to write past the bitmap buffer, crashing applications that mount it.

t: Dokploy 0.28.0 before 0.31.1 Path Traversal via patch.readRepoDirectories repoPath
d: Dokploy 0.28.0 before 0.31.1 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the patch.readRepoDirectories tRPC procedure that allows authenticated organization members to list tracked files of arbitrary git repositories. Attackers with service read permission can supply a crafted repoPath, which is passed to git ls-tree unconfined, to enumerate other organizations' application and compose source trees.

t: FFmpeg 7.0 through 9.0.2 Out-of-Bounds Read via dvdvideo_menu_next_ps_block()
d: FFmpeg 7.0 through 9.0.2 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in dvdvideo_menu_next_ps_block() in libavformat/dvdvideodec.c when demuxing DVD menu domains. Attackers can craft a DVD image whose last cell sector and NAV next-VOBU pointer bypass the end-of-cell check, overreading pgc->cell_playback and crashing the process.

t: Bar Assistant 3.0.0 before 6.11.0 Authorization Bypass via Null Invite Code
d: Bar Assistant 3.0.0 before 6.11.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in BarController::join that allows authenticated users to join bars without a valid invite code. Attackers can send POST requests to /api/bars/join omitting invite_code, matching invite-disabled bars with NULL codes, to read cocktails, ingredients, members, settings and search tokens.

t: Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via a declared element length passed unchecked to sysread in asn_read and asn_get
d: Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via a declared element length passed unchecked to sysread in asn_read and asn_get. The length an element declares in its BER header is passed to sysread as the read size. Perl grows the target buffer to that size before reading, so memory is allocated from the declared length, not from the data received. A 6-byte header can declare a length of up to 4GB. A single header makes the reading process allocate the declared size. Where the allocation fails, perl exits with "Out of memory", which eval cannot catch.

t: Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via unbounded arc length in OBJECT IDENTIFIER decoding and encoding
d: Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via unbounded arc length in OBJECT IDENTIFIER decoding and encoding. The content of an OBJECT IDENTIFIER or RELATIVE-OID element is passed to unpack "w*" on decode, and the arcs of an OID string to pack "w*" on encode. Perl converts each arc to or from its decimal string in time quadratic in the arc's length, and nothing limits that length. An attacker who controls the decoded data, or an OID string passed to encode, can exhaust CPU with a single oversized arc.

t: Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via unlimited recursion depth in constructed-form string decoding
d: Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via unlimited recursion depth in constructed-form string decoding. Any constructed-form string element causes the decoder to recurse on the element's contents. The BER encoding controls nesting depth at four bytes per level, with no bound checked. Perl recursion is heap-allocated, so the process grows without a stack crash. An attacker who controls the decoded data can exhaust memory with a small deeply nested constructed string.

t: Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via zero-length BIT STRING content
d: Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via zero-length BIT STRING content. A BIT STRING with zero content octets passes -1 to substr as the length. Perl reads a negative length as an offset from the end of the string, so the decoded value is nearly all of the input that follows the element. In the constructed form each zero-length segment copies the rest of the input again, so memory grows with the square of the input size. An attacker who controls the decoded data can exhaust memory with a short constructed BIT STRING. The resulting value also contains bytes from adjacent input.

t: Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via exponent-notation string in INTEGER encoding
d: Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via exponent-notation string in INTEGER encoding. The encoder routes any value with abs >= 2**31 to i2osp without validating that it is an integer. A string in exponent notation such as "1e8000" passes that threshold. Math::BigInt expands it to an 8001-digit integer, and i2osp's per-octet conversion loop is quadratic in that size. An attacker who controls encoded INTEGER values can exhaust CPU with a short exponent-notation string.

t: Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via unchecked exponent length in binary REAL decoding
d: Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via unchecked exponent length in binary REAL decoding. Binary REAL decoding never bounds-checks the exponent length against the available content. For a minimal one-byte binary REAL, the exponent byte is read from outside the element, making the mantissa length -1. Perl reads a negative length as an offset from the end of the string, so the mantissa is nearly all of the input that follows the element. The long-form exponent path also omits the extra length octet when sizing the mantissa. An attacker who controls the decoded data can exhaust CPU with a list of such values, as each mantissa loop iterates over the remaining input. The decoded values are also computed from bytes outside each element.

t: Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via unbounded MSG_PEEK buffer doubling in asn_recv
d: Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via unbounded MSG_PEEK buffer doubling in asn_recv. asn_recv peeks the socket in a loop, doubling the buffer size on each pass until a tag and length can be decoded. An inverted boolean guard ($tb || rather than $tb &&) prevents the need-more-data exit from firing once a tag byte has been decoded. When asn_decode_length returns no value because the length is absent or incomplete, no exit fires for that case either. MSG_PEEK leaves socket data unconsumed, so each re-peek returns at once while the buffer size doubles. A single truncated BER header sent to a process calling asn_recv doubles the peek buffer until memory is exhausted. Perl's realloc failure is fatal and not catchable with eval.

t: Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via quadratic bigint loop in os2ip
d: Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via quadratic bigint loop in os2ip. Every INTEGER or ENUMERATED longer than four content octets reaches os2ip, which iterates over each content octet with $result = ($result * 256) + $octet. Each multiplication operates on a bigint that grows by one octet per step, so decoding an n-octet value takes O(n^2) bigint work. Nothing limits content length before this loop runs. An attacker who controls the decoded data can exhaust CPU with a single oversized INTEGER or ENUMERATED value.

t: aoiflux mutant Forensic hive_builtins.go memory allocation
d: A vulnerability was determined in aoiflux mutant 2.3.0/2.4.0/2.5.0. This vulnerability affects unknown code of the file builtin/hive_builtins.go of the component Forensic Parser. This manipulation of the argument Count causes uncontrolled memory allocation. It is possible to launch the attack on the local host. Upgrading to version 2.6.0 is able to resolve this issue. Patch name: c4b1a7dec6c603115e2a05d1e8970a142f0b9774. Upgrading the affected component is recommended.

t: CVE-2026-22062 Information Exposure Vulnerability in StorageGRID (formerly StorageGRID Webscale)
d: StorageGRID (formerly StorageGRID Webscale) versions 12.1.0 and higher are susceptible to an information exposure vulnerability which allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to acquire low-sensitivity credentials via a Man-in-the-middle attack when certain non-default features are enabled.

t: Dolibarr ERP CRM Document Upload files.lib.php dol_convert_file code injection
d: A vulnerability was identified in Dolibarr ERP CRM up to 23.0.4. This affects the function dol_convert_file in the library htdocs/core/lib/files.lib.php of the component Document Upload. Such manipulation leads to code injection. The attack can be launched remotely. The exploit is publicly available and might be used. Upgrading to version 24.0.0 is able to mitigate this issue. The name of the patch is 9b6368b2a9eae3eec690b2ce22c4f291f0051540. Upgrading the affected component is advised.

t: WordPress PublishPress Authors plugin <= 4.18.0 - SQL Injection vulnerability
d: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection') vulnerability in PublishPress PublishPress Authors publishpress-authors allows Blind SQL Injection.This issue affects PublishPress Authors: from n/a through 4.18.0.

t: Org.keycloak:keycloak-model-jpa: case-variant realm urls bypass proxy restrictions
d: A flaw was found in Keycloak. When configured with a database that uses case-insensitive collation, Keycloak resolves realm URLs regardless of letter casing. A remote attacker can exploit this behavior by sending requests with alternate letter casing to bypass upstream reverse proxy access controls that rely on case-sensitive path matching. This issue can expose restricted authentication endpoints intended only for internal access, though Keycloak's internal authentication mechanisms remain intact.
Greenbone gvmd before 26.43.0 does not restrict certificate creation. Even the Observer role, documented to be read-only, can execute create_tls_certificate.

t: Keycloak: org.keycloak:keycloak-saml-adapter-core: org.keycloak:keycloak-saml-core: saml logoutrequest signature validation accepts a signed assertion nested in
d: A flaw was found in Keycloak. This vulnerability allows an authenticated remote attacker to cause a denial of service by terminating active sessions of arbitrary users. When processing Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) documents that lack a root signature, Keycloak accepts the request as long as any assertion within the document is signed, without verifying its context or placement. An attacker holding a validly signed assertion can embed it into an unsigned logout request for another user, causing Keycloak to accept the forged request and terminate the victim's session.

t: Etherpad: Pre-auth arbitrary file read
d: Etherpad is a real-time collaborative editor. From 1.8.14 until 3.3.3, the pre-authentication /static/* plugin asset handler in src/node/utils/Minify.ts performs a backslash-to-forward-slash conversion after src/node/utils/sanitizePathname.ts has completed its POSIX path checks. On POSIX systems the sanitizer correctly treats backslashes as ordinary filename bytes, but the later conversion turns encoded backslash-separated parent-directory segments into traversal components without revalidation or containment. The expressPreSession registration and the always-present ep_etherpad-lite core pseudo-plugin make this path reachable without credentials, allowing a remote attacker to read any file available to the Etherpad process. Disclosed configuration or environment secrets can expose administrator credentials, after which the administrator plugin installer can provide in-process code execution and full server compromise. This issue is fixed in version 3.3.3.

t: Flyto2 Core: SSRF guard bypass via DNS rebinding (validate_url_ssrf resolves-then-connects without pinning)
d: Flyto2 Core is an execution kernel for automation and AI-agent workflows. Prior to 2.26.8, validate_url_ssrf() in src/core/utils.py validates one DNS answer and then returns the hostname, while guarded_aiohttp_request(), enforce_outbound_url(), and validate_url_with_env_config() allow the outbound connection to perform an independent second lookup. A caller with control of the hostname's DNS can make validation see a public address and make the connection see an internal address, bypassing the guard across its outbound consumers and exposing readable internal or metadata-service responses. The attack requires low or zero DNS TTL behavior and a successful timing-dependent answer change; static multiple-address answers are checked and do not provide the same bypass. This issue is fixed in version 2.26.8.

t: Flyto2 Core: SSRF guard validates the resolved IP but connects by hostname, allowing DNS-rebinding TOCTOU
d: Flyto2 Core is an execution kernel for automation and AI-agent workflows. Prior to 2.26.8, validate_url_ssrf in src/core/utils.py resolves and checks a hostname but returns the hostname URL rather than the validated address, and session.get in http.get performs an independent DNS lookup when connecting. A low-privileged caller with control of the hostname's DNS can make the first lookup return a public address and the connection-time lookup return an internal address, bypassing the SSRF guard for all modules that call it and exposing readable internal or metadata-service responses. Successful exploitation requires attacker-controlled DNS and a successful timing-dependent answer change between the two lookups. This issue is fixed in version 2.26.8.

In Dolibarr before 24.0.3, /api/index.php/eventattendees discloses attendee and project data regardless of the caller's permissions. Only 22.0.0 and later (where api_eventattendees.class.php exists) are affected. A remote authenticated user can obtain column values one character at a time.

t: Flyto2 Core: Arbitrary file write via unguarded data.*/file.* modules (incomplete fix of CVE-2026-67429)
d: Flyto2 Core is an execution kernel for automation and AI-agent workflows. Prior to 2.26.8, the earlier CVE-2026-67429 remediation applied validate_path_with_env_config() to only a hand-picked set of file-writing modules, leaving data.csv.write in src/core/modules/atomic/data/csv_write.py, data.json_to_csv in src/core/modules/atomic/data/json_to_csv.py, file.copy in src/core/modules/atomic/file/copy.py, and file.move in src/core/modules/atomic/file/move.py outside the FLYTO_SANDBOX_DIR confinement boundary. The advisory also identifies unguarded modules across the broader data.*, file.*, and report-writer families. data.csv.write relies on a .. substring denylist that does not reject absolute paths, while the other named modules accept caller-controlled output or destination paths without the canonical guard. A caller able to execute modules or recipes can therefore write attacker-controlled content outside the configured sandbox, potentially overwriting application code, recipes, startup files, scheduled-task files, or authorization files and gaining code execution on the host. This issue is fixed in version 2.26.8.

t: Flyto2 Core: Path traversal in MCP `run_recipe` allows execution of workflows outside bundled recipe directory
d: Flyto2 Core is an execution kernel for automation and AI-agent workflows. Prior to 2.26.8, the MCP run_recipe tool in src/core/mcp_handler.py accepts a caller-controlled recipe_name that load_recipe() in src/cli/recipe.py appends to the src/recipes path without resolved-path containment. Parent-directory segments can therefore make Flyto load and execute a YAML workflow outside the bundled recipe directory, bypassing the boundary represented by list_recipes(). This does not necessarily provide unrestricted code execution because available workflow modules remain subject to Flyto's module policy, but it permits unintended execution of allowed browser, network, file, and data-processing modules. This issue is fixed in version 2.26.8.

t: Apache Tomcat: ExpiresFilter removes existing Cache-Control: private header
d: Use of cache containing sensitive information vulnerability in Apache Tomcat's ExpiresFilter caused by the filter removing cache-control header fields set by the authentication layer. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.27, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.61, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.123. The following versions were EOL at the time the CVE was created but are known to be affected: from 8.5.0 through 8.5.100, from 7.0.1 through 7.0.109. Older unsupported versions may also be affected. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.29, 10.1.62 or 9.0.124, which fix the issue. Note: Tomcat 11.0.28 was not released

t: Flyto2 Core: http.paginate follows server-supplied next-page URLs (Link header / cursor) without SSRF revalidation
d: Flyto2 Core is an execution kernel for automation and AI-agent workflows. Prior to 2.26.8, http.paginate in src/core/modules/atomic/http/paginate.py validates only the initial base_url, and _paginate_link_header then follows a server-supplied Link: rel="next" URL without calling the SSRF guard again. A low-privileged caller can make an allowed first page point the next request at an internal or metadata service, causing a readable second-order SSRF whose response body is aggregated into all_items and returned. This issue is fixed in version 2.26.8.

t: Apache Tomcat: Cluster TLS-PSK configured to use TLS 1.3 does not validate peer
d: Key exchange without entity authentication vulnerability in Apache Tomcat allowed an unauthenticated node to join a cluster when the cluster was secured with TLS 1.3 and TLS-PSK. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: 11.0.29, 10.1.62, 9.0.124. Users are recommended to switch to TLS 1.2 and PLDS-PSK or upgrade to version 11.0.30, 10.1.63 or 9.0.123 (when released), which fix the issue.

t: Apache Tomcat: CGIServlet drops chunked POST body and can hang worker thread
d: Allocation of resources without limits or throttling vulnerability in Apache Tomcat in the CGI Servlet when handling POST bodies can result in a DoS for some inputs. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.27, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.61, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.123. The following versions were EOL at the time the CVE was created but are known to be affected: from 8.5.0 through 8.5.100, from 7.0.0 through 7.0.109. Other unsupported versions may also be affected. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.29, 10.1.62 or 9.0.124, which fix the issue. Note: Tomcat 11.0.28 was not released

t: Apache Tomcat: Memory leak on HTTP upgrade leads to DoS
d: Allocation of resources without limits or throttling vulnerability in Apache Tomcat during HTTP upgrade in some circumstances lead to possible DoS. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.27, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.61, from 9.0.41 through 9.0.123. The following versions were EOL at the time the CVE was created but are known to be affected: from 8.5.61 through 8.5.100. Other unsupported versions may also be affected. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.29, 10.1.62 or 9.0.124, which fix the issue. Note: Tomcat 11.0.28 was not released

t: netty-incubator-codec-ohttp: OHTTP codecs retain consumed outer cumulation buffers after completed exchanges
d: netty-incubator-codec-ohttp implements Oblivious HTTP (OHTTP) gateway and client functionality using Netty. From 0.0.20.Final until 0.0.27.Final, OHttpClientCodec in codec-ohttp/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/ohttp/OHttpClientCodec.java and OHttpServerCodec in codec-ohttp/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/ohttp/OHttpServerCodec.java retain the consumed outer cumulationBuffer after a valid OHTTP exchange completes, even though OHttpRequestResponseContext.destroy in codec-ohttp/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/ohttp/OHttpRequestResponseContext.java releases the inner Binary HTTP cumulation and the channel remains active. A peer can complete a large request or response and leave the keep-alive connection idle, causing the client and server handlers to retain the current high-water pooled or direct buffer capacity until later inbound content replaces it or the handler is removed. Many long-lived idle connections can pin substantial memory and create availability pressure. The issue does not cause unbounded growth for repeated exchanges on a single channel. This issue is fixed in version 0.0.27.Final.

t: netty-incubator-codec-ohttp BinaryHttpParser: Unauthenticated CPU-exhaustion DoS via infinite loop in field-section decoding
d: netty-incubator-codec-ohttp implements Oblivious HTTP (OHTTP) gateway and client functionality using Netty. Prior to 0.0.23.Final, BinaryHttpParser.readFieldSection in codec-bhttp/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/bhttp/BinaryHttpParser.java loops while fieldSectionLength is nonzero and relies on disabled-by-default assertions to require BinaryHttpParser.readFieldLine to return a value and consume bytes. A corrupt field line can consume more bytes than its understated declared section length and drive the counter negative, or a truncated field line can return without consuming data and leave the parser in the same state. An unauthenticated OHTTP peer can encrypt such Binary HTTP content under the gateway public configuration, reach OHttpRequestResponseContext.ContentDecoder.decodeChunk, and permanently pin a Netty event-loop thread at full CPU before application business logic. Multiple requests can exhaust the event-loop group and deny service until restart. This issue is fixed in version 0.0.23.Final.

t: netty-incubator-codec-ohttp: BinaryHttpParser should enforce limits for variable lengths fields
d: netty-incubator-codec-ohttp implements Oblivious HTTP (OHTTP) gateway and client functionality using Netty. Prior to 0.0.23.Final, BinaryHttpParser does not enforce limits on encoded variable-length fields controlled by a remote peer. A remote peer can cause the decoder to buffer data indefinitely until memory is exhausted, causing denial of service. This issue is fixed in version 0.0.23.Final.

t: Apache Tomcat: RewriteValve [F]/[G]/[R] rule matches do not stop processing
d: Execution After Redirect (EAR) vulnerability in Apache Tomcat in RedirectValve affecting flags [F], [G] and [R]. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M18 through 11.0.27, from 10.1.20 through 10.1.61, from 9.0.87 through 9.0.123. The following versions were EOL at the time the CVE was created but are known to be affected: 8.5.100. Other unsupported versions may also be affected. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.29, 10.1.62, 9.0.124, which fixes the issue. Note: Tomcat 11.0.28 was not released

t: netty-incubator-codec-ohttp: Binary HTTP parser infinite loop on known-length field section boundary
d: netty-incubator-codec-ohttp implements Oblivious HTTP (OHTTP) gateway and client functionality using Netty. Prior to 0.0.23.Final, BinaryHttpParser.readFieldLine in codec-bhttp/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/bhttp/BinaryHttpParser.java treats a complete field line that ends exactly at a known field-section boundary as incomplete and returns without consuming bytes. BinaryHttpParser.readFieldSection then leaves fieldSectionLength unchanged and repeats the loop because its forward-progress checks are Java assertions, which are normally disabled in production. A remote peer that sends a known-length Binary HTTP header or trailer section ending at that boundary can make the parser spin indefinitely and pin the Netty event-loop or worker thread responsible for the channel. This issue is fixed in version 0.0.23.Final.

t: Apache Tomcat: Fix for CVE-2026-25854 was incomplete
d: The fix for CVE-2026-25854 was incomplete. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.19 through 11.0.27, from 10.1.53 through 10.1.61, from 9.0.116 through 9.0.123. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.29, 10.1.62 or 9.0.124, which fix the issue. Note: Tomcat 11.0.28 was not released

t: netty-incubator-codec-ohttp: BoringSSL HPKE private key bytes exposed through toString() and exception messages
d: netty-incubator-codec-ohttp implements Oblivious HTTP (OHTTP) gateway and client functionality using Netty. Prior to 0.0.23.Final, BoringSSLAsymmetricCipherKeyPair.toString in codec-ohttp-hpke-classes-boringssl/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/hpke/boringssl/BoringSSLAsymmetricCipherKeyPair.java includes its private parameter, BoringSSLAsymmetricKeyParameter.toString in codec-ohttp-hpke-classes-boringssl/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/hpke/boringssl/BoringSSLAsymmetricKeyParameter.java renders the complete private-key byte array when isPrivate is true, and BoringSSL.EVP_HPKE_KEY_init_or_throw in codec-ohttp-hpke-classes-boringssl/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/hpke/boringssl/BoringSSL.java includes rejected privateKeyBytes in an exception message. Applications that log affected key-pair objects or initialization exceptions can persist complete HPKE private key material in logs or telemetry. Anyone who can read those records can recover the key and may compromise OHTTP message confidentiality or authenticity expectations while the key remains usable. This issue is fixed in version 0.0.23.Final.

In Dolibarr before 24.0.3, dolForgeSQLCriteriaCallback() in htdocs/core/lib/functions.lib.php allows account takeover because it strips only a single table-name prefix from a Universal Search Filter (sqlfilters) operand before checking it against the forbidden-field denylist (pass, pass_crypted, api_key). MariaDB and MySQL accept a two-level qualification such as schema.alias.column, so an operand of the form dolibarr.u.pass_crypted survives the check and is emitted into the WHERE clause. A remote authenticated user holding only the holiday read and readall permissions, which confer no user-management or administrative access, can use the resulting boolean oracle at GET /api/index.php/holidays to recover any user's bcrypt password hash and api_key one character at a time, including an administrator's. Because api_key is accepted directly by the REST API as a bearer credential, this yields full administrative control of the application. This bypasses the fix for CVE-2026-89012, which added only a strtolower() call and did not address prefix depth. The same denylist also omits pass_temp, which stores a password in cleartext, as well as national_registration_number, salary, birth, address, personal_mobile and note_private.

t: Apache Tomcat: HTTP/2 checks frame type before size leads to DoS
d: Missing release of resource after effective lifetime vulnerability in Apache Tomcat's HTTP/2 initial connection handling leads to DoS. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.27, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.61, from 9.0.20 through 9.0.123. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.29, 10.1.62 or 9.0.124, which fix the issue. Note: Tomcat 11.0.28 was not released

t: netty-incubator-codec-ohttp: Binary HTTP parser unchecked varint length overflow causes decoder crash
d: netty-incubator-codec-ohttp implements Oblivious HTTP (OHTTP) gateway and client functionality using Netty. Prior to 0.0.23.Final, BinaryHttpParser in codec-bhttp/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/bhttp/BinaryHttpParser.java accumulates attacker-controlled Binary HTTP variable-length integers into the int offset sumBytes. BinaryHttpParser.readRequestHead, BinaryHttpParser.readFieldLine, and BinaryHttpParser.getIndeterminateLength can narrow long lengths into that offset, causing integer wraparound before buffer indices are calculated. A remote peer that supplies a valid large encoded length to BinaryHttpParser or BinaryHttpDecoder can trigger an unchecked bounds exception from a small malformed message, fail or close the channel, and repeatedly cause denial of service. Java and Netty bounds checks prevent memory corruption, and no information disclosure was observed. This issue is fixed in version 0.0.23.Final.

t: Apache Tomcat: Memory leak with OWB integration leads to DoS
d: Missing release of memory after effective lifetime vulnerability in Apache Tomcat via WebSocket. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.27, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.61, from 9.0.22 through 9.0.123 The following versions were EOL at the time the CVE was created but are known to be affected: from 8.5.0 through 8.5.100, from 7.0.43 through 7.0.109. Other unsupported versions may also be affected. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.29, 10.0.62 or 9.0.124, which fix the issue. Note: Tomcat 11.0.28 was not released

t: Apache Tomcat: Jakarta Authentication secureResponse AuthException sends unprotected HTTP 200 response
d: Improper cleanup on thrown exception vulnerability in Apache Tomcat meant that an HTTP 200 response was sent rather than an HTTP 500 response after a AuthException was thrown during Jakarta Authentication secureResponse(). This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.27, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.61, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.123. The following versions were EOL at the time the CVE was created but are known to be affected: from 8.5.0 through 8.5.100. Other unsupported versions may also be affected. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.29, 10.0.62 or 9.0.124, which fix the issue. Note: Tomcat 11.0.28 was not released

t: Apache Tomcat: Incorrect security-role-ref with RequestDispatcher.forward()
d: Incorrect Authorization vulnerability in Apache Tomcat could occur during a request dispatch if the request depended on a security-role-ref provided by the dispatch target. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.27, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.61, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.123. The following versions were EOL at the time the CVE was created but are known to be affected: from 8.5.0 through 8.5.100, from 7.0.0 through 7.0.109. Other unsupported versions may also be affected. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.29, 10.1.62 or 9.0.124, which fixes the issue. Note: Tomcat 11.0.28 was not released

t: Apache Tomcat: Multiple vulnerabilities in EncryptInterceptor
d: Reliance on obfuscation or encryption of Security-Relevant inputs without integrity checking, Improper validation of integrity check value, Cleartext transmission of sensitive information vulnerability in the EncryptInterceptor of Apache Tomcat. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.27, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.61, from 9.0.13 through 9.0.123. The following versions were EOL at the time the CVE was created but are known to be affected: from 8.5.38 through 8.5.100, from 7.0.100 through 7.0.109. Other unsupported versions may also be affected. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.29, 10.1.62 or 9.0.124 and switch to TLS-PSK to encrypt cluster communication, which fixes the issue. Note: Tomcat 11.0.28 was not released

t: OSGeo shapelib dbfopen.c DBFCloneEmpty null pointer dereference
d: A weakness has been identified in OSGeo shapelib up to 1.6.3. This vulnerability affects the function DBFCloneEmpty of the file dbfopen.c. This manipulation causes null pointer dereference. It is possible to launch the attack on the local host. Patch name: f79050a900d2a05529501b2b714b8f89067db071. It is recommended to apply a patch to fix this issue.

t: IBM API Connect Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key
d: IBM API Connect 10.0.8.0 through 10.0.8.13 could allow a remote authenticated attacker to delete API keys belonging to other users due to improper authorization checks.

t: Multiple Vulnerabilities in watsonx.data
d: IBM watsonx.data 2.4.0 through 2.4.0 patch 8 does not invalidate session after a logout which could allow an authenticated user to impersonate another user on the system.

t: API Authentication and Rule Generation in the Auth0 Authorization Extension
d: In the Auth0 Authorization Extension, request authentication handling can process claims from query parameters independently of header validation. Under specific preconditions, this may allow an authenticated tenant user to issue requests to the extension's administrative endpoints. Also, input handling during rule generation may permit modification of the tenant login rule published by the extension.

t: Multiple Vulnerabilities in watsonx.data
d: IBM watsonx.data 2.4.0 through 2.4.0 patch 8 could allow unauthorized network access due to insufficient network segmentation controls.

t: Multiple Vulnerabilities in watsonx.data
d: IBM watsonx.data 2.4.0 through 2.4.0 patch 8 could allow a remote attacker to obtain sensitive information due to improper access control.

t: Multiple Vulnerabilities in watsonx.data
d: IBM watsonx.data 2.4.0 through 2.4.0 patch 8 could allow a local attacker to obtain sensitive credentials due to the use of a hard-coded cryptographic key.

t: Multiple Vulnerabilities in watsonx.data
d: IBM watsonx.data 2.4.0 through 2.4.0 patch 8 could allow a remote authenticated attacker to cause a denial of service due to client-side enforcement of business rules.

t: Multiple Vulnerabilities in watsonx.data
d: IBM watsonx.data 2.4.0 through 2.4.0 patch 8 could allow a remote authenticated attacker to conduct a server-side request forgery due to a server-side request forgery (SSRF) vulnerability.

t: Improper Request URL Validation in the Okta .NET SDK Abstractions Library
d: In the Okta .NET SDK Abstractions library, outbound HTTP requests are not restricted to the configured Okta organization domain when processing certain URL formats. If a URL parameter is modified to specify an external host, the library may transmit the configured SSWS API token to that unintended destination.

t: Path Parameter Encoding in Okta Swift Management SDK
d: The Okta Swift Management SDK does not percent-encode forward slash (/) characters during path parameter interpolation. If an application supplies input containing relative path sequences (e.g., ../) to an SDK method, standard URL normalization may direct the outbound request to an alternative Okta Management API endpoint.

t: Improper Synchronization in the Okta .NET SDK Abstractions Library
d: The Okta .NET SDK Abstractions library improperly synchronizes authentication credentials set on a shared HTTP client during request execution. When concurrent requests are dispatched for different principals, one principal's credential may be transmitted on an outbound request intended for another principal, which can result in credential exposure and lead to unauthorized actions performed as the affected principal at the Okta Management API.

t: Credential Overwriting in Okta .NET SDK Abstractions Library
d: The Okta .NET SDK Abstractions library systematically writes per-request authentication credentials to a shared HTTP client instance, rather than being isolated to individual outbound request objects. When using scoped child clients, a subsequent scoped request can overwrite the shared client configuration. Because the original parent client credential has not been restored, subsequent outbound requests may be transmitted using the newly written credential, which can result in subsequent actions being executed under the context of an incorrect security principal in the Okta Management API and improper attribution in audit logs.

t: Front-Channel Parameter Handling in Okta Client SDK for Python
d: The Okta Client SDK for Python (okta-client-python) includes client authentication values (client_secret or JWT assertions) as query parameters in the front-channel authorization URL when executing the authorization code flow without Pushed Authorization Requests (PAR). When PAR is disabled, unsupported by the authorization server, or fails, the SDK falls back to standard authorization URL construction, transmitting these parameters via user-agent requests.

t: FreeRDP Smartcard Redirection Memory Handling in Okta Privileged Access Gateway
d: Okta Privileged Access (OPA) Gateway includes a version of the FreeRDP library affected by memory management issues in its smartcard redirection handling. When an RDP session is established meeting specific session criteria, command execution within the context of the local Gateway service account may be allowed.

t: Symbolic Link Resolution in Okta Verify for macOS
d: On Intel-based macOS systems, the Okta Device Access (ODA) component of Okta Verify for macOS configures a LaunchDaemon service whose program path resolves via a symbolic link in /usr/local/bin. In environments where non-standard directory permissions grant local non-root users write access to this path, the symbolic link target can be modified, causing the LaunchDaemon to execute the replacement binary upon service restart.

t: IBM Guardium Data Protection Missing Authentication
d: IBM Guardium Data Protection 12.2 is vulnerable to missing authentication in the SharePoint S-TAP RelayService, allowing an unauthenticated network attacker to inject forged audit events and access the active monitoring policy.

t: GCM authentication tag length downgrade in Amazon S3 Encryption Client for PHP
d: Insufficient verification of data authenticity in the decryption component of Amazon S3 Encryption Client for PHP in AWS SDK for PHP before 3.383.1 might allow an authenticated remote user to forge ciphertext that decrypts to arbitrary plaintext via manipulation of the GCM authentication tag length metadata. To remediate this issue, users should upgrade to AWS SDK for PHP version 3.383.1 or later.

t: IBM Guardium Data Protection Buffer Overflow
d: IBM Guardium Data Protection 12.2 is vulnerable to a stack-based buffer overflow when processing a specially crafted PROXY protocol v1 header. A remote attacker can exploit this vulnerability to cause a denial of service or potentially execute arbitrary code.

t: IBM Guardium Data Protection Out-of-bounds Read
d: IBM Guardium Data Protection 12.2 could allow a remote attacker to obtain sensitive information or cause a denial of service due to an out-of-bounds heap read.

t: IBM Guardium Data Protection Improper Privilege Management
d: IBM Guardium Data Protection 12.2 is vulnerable to local privilege escalation via the SUID-root podman_wrapper binary on the Collector appliance. A local attacker with low-privileged access to the Collector can exploit insufficient argument validation in the SUID binary to execute arbitrary commands as root, resulting in full compromise of the Collector appliance.

t: IBM Guardium Data Protection Improper Output Neutralization for Logs
d: IBM Guardium Data Protection 12.2 could allow a remote attacker to inject forged audit records due to improper output neutralization for logs.

t: IBM Guardium Data Protection Deserialization of Untrusted Data
d: IBM Guardium Data Protection 12.2 is vulnerable to insecure deserialization in the SharePoint Tap MulticastTransceiver component. An unauthenticated remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability to execute arbitrary code on the affected system.

t: IBM Guardium Data Protection Path Traversal
d: IBM Guardium Data Protection 12.2 is vulnerable to path traversal in the datasource functionality. An authenticated attacker could exploit this vulnerability to delete arbitrary files on the appliance.

t: IBM Guardium Data Protection Improper Certificate Validation
d: IBM Guardium Data Protection 12.2 is vulnerable to improper TLS certificate validation in the GDP Terraform provider, allowing a network attacker with a man-in-the-middle position to intercept sensitive credentials transmitted to the Guardium appliance.

t: IBM Guardium Data Protection SQL Injection
d: IBM Guardium Data Protection 12.2 is vulnerable to SQL injection in the edge-controller component. An unauthenticated remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability to access or modify sensitive database information.
